1	You are adjudicating disagreements between a benchmark case's answer key and an independent expert's blind solution. For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to a substantive (not merely evidence-gathering) intervention? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.
9	
10	Truth convention: expected answers are what a careful analyst concludes after reading the initial file plus the optimal read path (at most three catalogue items); for INCOMPLETE and NOCONC cases, what the whole catalogue supports.

318	CASE OD2-DEV-CONFOUND (CONFOUND, cross-domain): The tutoring program whose students score lower
319	Setting: Pellham Ridge Unified School District (fictional) runs five middle schools (Ashgrove, Corliss, Dunmore, Fenwick, Halvard) with about 3,100 students in grades 6–8. Since October 2025 it has run Bridge Hours, an after-school small-group math tutoring program staffed by a contractor, Northgate Learning Partners, at a cost of $640,000 a year. The board votes on 12 March 2026 whether to renew, cut or expand the Northgate contract. A new board dashboard compares winter benchmark scores of Bridge Hours participants with those of non-participants.
320	Presenting request: Superintendent Abel Kruger: 'Trustee Venter will move to end Bridge Hours at the March 12 budget meeting because the dashboard shows participants scoring far below everyone else. Northgate says the program is working and wants it expanded. I need to know what that score gap actually means and what I should recommend to the board.'
321	INITIAL EVIDENCE
322	E1 [stage S1] Email from Trustee Marisol Venter to the superintendent and board, 2 Feb 2026 (leadership-account): Subject: Bridge Hours. The winter benchmark dashboard settles this. Bridge Hours students averaged 198.0; everyone else averaged 224.4. That's a 26-point gap, and it shows up at every one of our five middle schools. We are paying Northgate $640,000 a year for a program whose students do worse than kids who never set foot in it. Teachers tell me the tutors teach tricks that contradict what's taught in class. At the March 12 budget meeting I will move that we end the Northgate contract and return the money to the general fund.
323	E2 [stage S1] Board dashboard, Grade 6–8 Math, winter benchmark (system-record): Board Dashboard — Grade 6–8 Math, Winter Benchmark (administered 12–16 Jan 2026). Bridge Hours participants: n=412, mean scale score 198.0. Non-participants: n=2,694, mean 224.4. Gap (participants minus non-participants) by school: Ashgrove −23.0; Corliss −29.1; Dunmore −22.6; Fenwick −27.4; Halvard −28.7. Proficient (scale ≥ 220): participants 9%, non-participants 58%. Footnote: 'Participant' = enrolled in Bridge Hours on 1 Dec 2025. Scale range 140–300. All students in a grade took the same winter form.
324	E3 [stage S1] Bridge Hours Program Overview 2025–26, district website (document): Bridge Hours offers small-group math tutoring (up to five students per tutor) for grades 6–8 at all five middle schools. Sessions run Tuesdays and Thursdays, 3:35–4:35 p.m., after the 3:15 dismissal bell, from 14 October to 30 April. Tutors are employed by Northgate Learning Partners under contract and use Northgate's 'Stepwise' lesson sets. Students join through school referral; families must return a consent form. A late bus takes participants home. Contact your school's Bridge Hours site coordinator for details.
325	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, grade 7 math teacher, Corliss Middle, taken by a board aide, 28 Jan 2026 (staff-account): 'Two or three of my Bridge kids came back comparing fractions by cross-multiplying when I'd taught common denominators, and one mixed the two methods up on the December quiz. I mentioned it to the tutor; she said they show both ways.' Asked whether Bridge Hours was hurting scores: 'I honestly couldn't say. The kids in Bridge are mostly the ones I was already worried about in September, so I'd expect them to be lower either way. Some of them do seem more willing to try now.'
326	E5 [stage S1] Email from Renata Osei, Regional Director, Northgate Learning Partners, to the superintendent, 3 Feb 2026 (vendor-account): Our tracking shows Bridge Hours students gained 15 scale points from the fall diagnostic to the winter benchmark, versus 9 points for non-participants — roughly two-thirds more growth. The dashboard's raw comparison is unfair to the program. We recommend expanding Bridge Hours to grades 4–5 next year. We would also suggest ending the district's referral list and opening sign-up to any interested student, which would give a more representative picture of what Bridge Hours can achieve.
327	CATALOGUE (full contents)
328	C1 [stage S1] Fall diagnostic (September 2025) results by Bridge Hours enrollment status - District assessment system extract, run 9 Feb 2026 (system-record): Fall math diagnostic administered 15–19 Sep 2025; results released to schools 26 Sep. Bridge Hours participants (n=412): fall mean 182.8; 374 (91%) scored below 196, the district 40th percentile. Non-participants (n=2,694): fall mean 215.1; 328 (12%) scored below 196. Mean fall-to-winter change: participants +15.3, non-participants +9.4. Across all students regardless of enrollment, those scoring below 196 in the fall gained an average of 15.5 points by winter; those scoring 196 or above gained 8.6 points.
329	C2 [stage S1] Bridge Hours referral and enrollment procedure, 2025–26 - Office of Academic Services, Procedure AS-14 (rev. Aug 2025) (document): 1. Under the state supplemental-intervention rule, every grade 6–8 student scoring below the district 40th percentile on the fall math diagnostic (scale 196 for 2025–26) must be offered a documented supplemental math intervention. 2. Bridge Hours is the district's designated intervention for grades 6–8 math for 2025–26; any replacement must be designated by the board before the school year begins. 3. Once diagnostic results are released, the district office sends each school a referral list of all students below the cut; site coordinators contact every family on it. 4. Teachers may refer students at or above the cut with principal approval, space permitting. 5. Enrollment opens 6 October.
330	C3 [stage S1] Research office analysis of winter benchmark results by fall diagnostic band - Memo, Research & Accountability Office, 10 Feb 2026 (document): Winter means by fall-diagnostic band, participants (P) vs non-participants (N). Below 180: P n=161, 190.1; N n=118, 191.7. 180–195: P n=213, 201.5; N n=210, 203.8. 196–210: P n=31, 209.9; N n=604, 213.0. Above 210: P n=7 (not reported); N n=1,762, 233.0. Fall-to-winter growth, P vs N, first three bands: +18.1 vs +17.2; +14.0 vs +14.2; +10.9 vs +10.2. Within each band, participants started 2.1–3.8 points lower in the fall. Among non-participants each fall point predicts about 0.7 winter points, so starting differences explain most within-band gaps; remainders are under one point, one positive and two negative. This design cannot detect a small Bridge Hours effect in either direction. A comparison of students just either side of the 196 cut can be ready by 27 Feb. Session attendance has not been linked to scores.
331	C4 [stage S1] Bridge Hours session attendance logs, 14 Oct – 18 Dec 2025 - Northgate attendance system export (log): All five sites. 412 enrolled students; 18 sessions offered per student in the period. Median attendance 11.5 of 18 sessions (64%). 71 students attended fewer than 5 sessions; 96 attended 16 or more. Site attendance ranged from 58% (Dunmore) to 71% (Fenwick). Recorded absence reasons: 'no show / no reason given' 52%, 'late bus conflict' 17%, 'sports/activities' 14%, other 17%. Export fields: student ID, session date, status. No assessment data included.
332	C5 [stage S1] Northgate Stepwise curriculum alignment statement and sample fraction lesson - Northgate Learning Partners program document, Sept 2025 (vendor-account): 'Stepwise lesson sets are fully aligned to state grade 6–8 math standards and to partner districts' scope and sequence.' Sample lesson 3.2, Comparing Fractions: tutors model the common-denominator method first, then a 'Quick Check: cross-multiply to confirm.' Tutor note in margin: 'If the student's teacher uses a different method, follow the teacher's method.' The statement does not name Pellham Ridge's textbook, and the district-reviewer signature line on the alignment page is blank.
333	C6 [stage S1] Winter benchmark technical bulletin from the assessment vendor - Assessment vendor technical bulletin, Jan 2026 (vendor-account): Winter grade 6–8 math form W-3 administered district-wide 12–16 Jan 2026; one form per grade for all students. Reported reliability 0.91. The fall diagnostic and the winter benchmark are reported on a common vertical scale. Testing accommodations used by 11% of students district-wide. Make-up window 20–23 Jan; 2.4% of students tested in the make-up window. No scoring or administration incidents logged for Pellham Ridge.
334	C7 [stage S1] Northgate contract and Bridge Hours budget, 2025–26 - District finance office, contract file NLP-2025-031 (financial-record): Annual contract value $640,000: tutor wages and Northgate overhead $548,000; materials $34,000; late-bus transportation $58,000 (district-run, charged to program budget). Cost per enrolled student about $1,553. Term ends 30 June 2026; renewal requires board approval. Either party may terminate for convenience with 60 days' written notice. Invoices paid through January 2026 total $318,400.
335	C8 [stage S1] Bridge Hours family satisfaction survey, December 2025 - Northgate-administered family survey (customer-account): 188 of 412 families responded (46%). 79% 'satisfied' or 'very satisfied'. 71% say their child is 'more confident in math'. 22% cite late-bus timing as a problem. Sample comments: 'She actually asks for help now'; 'Sessions sometimes start ten minutes late'; 'Wish there was homework help too.' The survey did not ask about grades or test scores.
336	C9 [stage S1] Spring 2025 state math test results for students enrolled in Bridge Hours in 2025–26 - District data warehouse extract, 9 Feb 2026 (system-record): Students with a spring 2025 state math result (then in grades 5–7). 2025–26 Bridge Hours participants: n=396; 81% scored 'below standard' (level 1 or 2 of 4); mean performance level 1.8. 2025–26 non-participants: n=2,601; 29% below standard; mean level 2.9. Sixteen participants and 93 non-participants had no prior-year result (new to the district).
337	C10 [stage S1] Interview with the Bridge Hours site coordinator, Dunmore Middle - Interview notes, 5 Feb 2026 (staff-account): 'In late September the district office sends us a list — everyone under the cut on the fall diagnostic. We call every family on it. About half say yes; the ones who don't usually mention sports, a sibling to pick up, or just aren't interested. A few teachers add kids who are just over the line. So Bridge is basically the kids who were struggling in September.' On Northgate's idea of open sign-up: 'We'd fill up with kids who'd be fine anyway, and the list kids would lose seats.'
338	C11 [stage S1] Northgate tutor roster and turnover, Oct 2025 – Jan 2026 - Northgate staffing report to the district (system-record): 24 tutors at program start; 3 departures (two in December, one in January), each replaced within 8 school days. Of the current 24, 19 hold a bachelor's degree in a STEM field or education and 6 hold teaching certificates. Average tutor-to-student ratio 1:4.3. Training: 12 hours pre-service plus 2 hours monthly.
339	C12 [stage S1] News coverage of tutoring program results in neighbouring districts - Valley Courier, 22 Jan 2026 (external-data): 'In Ostrander County schools, students in after-school reading tutoring scored lower on fall benchmarks than their classmates, prompting one board member to call the program a waste. District officials said the tutoring is aimed at struggling readers.' The article reports no further analysis. Ostrander's program uses a different vendor and serves grades 2–5 reading.
340	CANDIDATES
341	H1: Bridge Hours tutoring is the main reason participants score lower than non-participants on the winter benchmark.
342	H2: Bridge Hours enrolls mainly students who were already scoring low before tutoring began, and this prior-achievement difference accounts for most of the winter score gap.
343	H3: Conflicts between Northgate's Stepwise methods and classroom methods are depressing participants' benchmark scores to some degree.
344	H4: Bridge Hours sessions take time away from participants' regular math instruction.
